reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial provides strong evidence of target engagement through PK data showing ADC (brentuximab vedotin) exposure with Cmax of 36.95 μg/mL in cycle 1 and 32.43 μg/mL in cycle 2, along with MMAE (the cytotoxic payload) exposure with Cmax of 5.16 μg/mL in cycle 1 and 3.62 μg/mL in cycle 2. The development of anti-therapeutic antibodies (ATA) in 8/38 participants further confirms drug exposure and immune recognition of the ADC. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: While direct pathway biomarkers aren't reported, the mechanism of antibody-drug conjugate cytotoxicity was demonstrated through the clinical response pattern. The differential response rates between disease subtypes (CR rate 55.6% in sALCL vs 20.0% in HL) suggests CD30-mediated targeting and payload delivery occurred as intended. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was clearly met with an overall response rate of 70%, which is clinically meaningful for relapsed/refractory CD30-positive lymphomas. The high response rates in both Hodgkin lymphoma and systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma demonstrate clinical benefit. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial showed differential responses between disease subtypes, with sALCL showing higher complete response rates (55.6%) compared to Hodgkin lymphoma (20.0%), and better B symptom resolution (100% vs 50%), suggesting the mechanism may be more effective in certain CD30-positive malignancies. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was a single-arm trial without a control group, but the response rates are well above historical benchmarks for these relapsed/refractory populations. The safety profile was manageable with expected hematologic toxicities.

failure_modes.evidence: Single-arm design limits ability to definitively establish efficacy compared to standard of care, though response rates exceed historical benchmarks
